question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{(3n-2)(3n+2)}{n(1-9n)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(3n-2)(3n+2)}{n(1-9n)}=\frac{9{n}^{2}-4}{n-9{n}^{2}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{9{n}^{2}-4}{n-9{n}^{2}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-9{n}^{2},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{9{n}^{2}-4}{n-9{n}^{2}} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{4}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{n}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{9{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(9-\frac{4}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{1}{n}-9)} \\  & =\frac{9-0}{0-9} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $-1.$
